title: SCE Crews Stay Ready for Extreme Heat
summary: With Southern California under an extreme heat warning over several continuous days, SCE crews prepare to respond to potential outages.
body_markdown:
Though fall is here, California weather hasn’t gotten the memo — extreme heat is spreading across the state.


The[National Weather Service](https://www.weather.gov/) issued an[extreme heat watch](https://forecast.weather.gov/wwamap/wwatxtget.php?cwa=usa&wwa=Extreme%20Heat%20Watch) across most of Southern California Edison’s service area for several continuous days. Temperatures are expected to climb into triple digits from Friday through Thursday, Oct. 8. Coastal communities are forecast to see temperatures hit the upper 90s while valley communities may experience up to 105 degrees or higher.


As temperatures increase, so do people’s use of air conditioning — giving homes, businesses and electrical equipment little opportunity to cool down. That combination can place added stress on the electric grid, which may increase the potential of heat-related outages.


[SCE crews](https://energized.edison.com/stories/lineworkers-share-safety-tips-for-extreme-heat) are keeping a close eye on conditions and are ready to help restore power as safely and quickly as possible should customers experience any heat-related outages. Customers can check the latest outage information at[sce.com/outages](https://www.sce.com/outages-safety?from=/outages) .
